title: Spannagel Cave at the Hintertux Glacier
name: Spannagel Cave at the Hintertux Glacier
kurzbeschreibung: Spannagelhöhle at Hintertuxer Gletscher at 2,521 m: Europe's highest show cave and the largest marble cave in the Central Alps with 13 km of passageways.
beschreibung:
Overview

The geologically fascinating Spannagelhöhle is situated at an altitude of 2,521 metres directly adjacent to the historic Spannagelhaus at Hintertuxer Gletscher in the municipality of Tux in the Zillertal (Bezirk Schwaz). With an explored total length exceeding 13 kilometres, this subterranean natural monument is the largest cave system in the entire Central Alps and simultaneously Europe's highest show cave. Its distinctive feature lies in its geology: while most large caves occur in limestone mountains, Spannagelhöhle is a unique geological phenomenon carved deep into a massive band of crystalline primitive marble.

Marble Labyrinths & Show Cave Tour

On the approximately one-hour, electrically illuminated show cave tour, visitors accompanied by certified cave guides explore some 500 metres into the mountain wearing hard hats and headlamps. The subterranean interior reveals an intriguing wonderland: deep black and pure white bands of marble alternate, smoothly polished giant's kettles (swirl pools) bear witness to the powerful torrents of past ice ages, and delicate speleothems (stalactites and stalagmites) grow slowly in the cool cave environment. Information boards and exhibits in the integrated Höhlenmuseum shed light on the cave's discovery in 1919, alpine bat species, and rare mineral finds. For adventurous guests, demanding trekking expeditions into undeveloped branches of the cave system are offered.

Visit & Getting There

Spannagelhöhle is open to visitors year-round; regular guided tours take place daily on the hour from 10:00 to 15:00. The temperature inside remains constant at around 2 °C in both summer and winter. Admission prices including guided tour and rental gear (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €16.00, children (6 to 14 years) approx. €9.00. Access is easy via the glacier cable cars (Gletscherbus 1 and 2) from Hintertux up to the Tuxer Fernerhaus station (2,660 m), from where a gentle ten-minute walk downhill leads to the cave entrance. Getting there: via the B169 and Tuxer Landesstraße to the Hintertux valley station (large free car park).

Tips

Sturdy closed hiking boots and warm mountain clothing are essential for visiting the cave. The show cave is well secured with stairs and fortified paths, but is not barrier-free due to rock steps. After the tour, stop by the rustic Spannagelhaus and enjoy traditional Zillertaler Kasspatzln cheese spaetzle on the sun terrace.
